questions.stem: A 25-year-old footballer was injured while heading a ball. He was unconscious for less than a minute and then continued to play. At the end of the game he felt drowsy and was brought to the emergency department unable to be aroused, with a Glasgow Coma Score of 13. A CT scan shows an extradural haemorrhage. Rupture of which blood vessel has caused the extradural haematoma?
questions.explanation: The middle meningeal artery enters the skull via the foramen spinosum and lies in a groove on the temporal bone. Fracture in this region can tear the artery, causing extradural haemorrhage.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman with an untreated infected lesion on her face complains of severe ocular pain, fever and chemosis, and has a pulsating proptosis. Which one of the following structures is involved?
questions.explanation: The cavernous sinus is vulnerable to thrombosis from facial infections in the “danger area” of the face. This can cause ocular pain, chemosis, proptosis and ophthalmoplegia.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man, a smoker, presents with intermittent amaurosis fugax, a typical carotid bruit on the same side. He has a systolic carotid bruit on the same side. The main artery that is affected enters the orbit through which one of the following foramina?
questions.explanation: The central artery of the retina is a branch of the ophthalmic artery, which enters the orbit through the optic canal with the optic nerve.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman is diagnosed with a space-occupying lesion at the cerebellopontine angle. The lesion is arising from which one of the following structures?
questions.explanation: Cerebellopontine angle tumours are usually acoustic neuromas arising from the vestibulocochlear nerve at the auditory meatus.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man presents with sudden onset of severe thunderclap headache, which he likens to a “hammer blow” to the back of the head. A gadolinium-enhanced MRI shows a haemorrhagic lesion in the anterior cranial fossa. Which one of the following vessels is involved?
questions.explanation: A ruptured berry aneurysm commonly occurs at the anterior communicating artery and presents with subarachnoid haemorrhage.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man, after investigations for persistent early morning headaches, is found to have raised intracranial pressure from a pituitary adenoma. Recently he finds that he is bumping into the sides of doorways and people. Pressure by the tumour into which of the following structures is causing the specific visual problem?
questions.explanation: Pituitary adenoma compresses the optic chiasma, affecting nasal retinal fibres and causing bitemporal hemianopia.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man, a recent immigrant from Africa, presents with an advanced right-sided nasopharyngeal carcinoma. A CT scan shows widespread destruction into the right posterior fossa at the base of the skull. On protruding the tongue, it deviates towards the side of the lesion. Which one of the following nerves is affected by the growth?
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal nerve exits through the hypoglossal canal and supplies the intrinsic and extrinsic muscles of the tongue. Lesion causes deviation of the tongue towards the affected side.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man presents with anosmia, after sustaining a fracture of his anterior cranial fossa in a road traffic accident 5 weeks ago. At that time he had cerebrospinal rhinorrhoea. Fracture of which one of the following bones is causing his anosmia?
options: Cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone
Frontal process of the zygomatic bone
Orbital plate of the frontal bone
Squamous part of the temporal bone
questions.explanation: Olfactory nerve fibres pass through the cribriform plate. Fracture here can damage the olfactory bulbs and cause anosmia and cerebrospinal rhinorrhoea.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition
